test.name: Two sources disagreeing about the same fact routes to conflict-resolution
test.description: Boundary against conflict-resolution. The user describes two sources giving different answers for one fact -- that is a conflict to be weighed, not a defect in a source to be classified. source-evaluation asks whether a source belongs here and whether it was indexed correctly; conflict-resolution asks which of two sources to believe. One-directional by design: the reciprocal under eval/tests/unit/conflict-resolution/ would arm that suite's runlog gate, which is already red from 312d3c670 deleting its references/validation-protocol.md. check_negative_reciprocity.py warns on this edge; the warning is expected.

input.user_message: The 1900 census says Christian was born in 1875 and the 1885 state census says 1852 -- which one should I believe?

negative.explanation: The user is not asking whether the sources belong on the profile or whether they were indexed correctly -- they are asking which of two disagreeing sources to believe. That is independence analysis and the preponderance hierarchy, which conflict-resolution owns. source-evaluation's own body routes this case away in its first section.

judge_context: Should route to conflict-resolution and produce no audit of its own
Should not call person_read, record_read or source_attachments
The handoff is silent -- source-evaluation writes no reply of its own
